summary: Changed src/humanize/lists.py so natural_list accepts any iterable. Added `from collections.abc import Iterable` inside the existing `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block next to `Any`, annotated the parameter as `items: Iterable[Any]`, and updated the docstring to 'Convert an iterable of items' with `items (Iterable): An iterable of items.` The body now first builds `item_list = [str(item) for item in items]` and works only on that list (empty -> "", one -> the item, two -> `f"{a} and {b}"`, more -> last joined with `", "` then `f" and {last}"`). This makes tuples, dict views, generators and ranges work correctly via a single pass. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_lists.py` passes: 14 passed.
concerns: Output for plain lists should remain byte-identical to before (spot-checked via the tests).
The `Iterable` and `Any` imports live under TYPE_CHECKING since `from __future__ import annotations` is present, so runtime behavior is unaffected.
